annotations.title: Buscar empresas que usam um ERP

description: Finds companies that run one of the ERPs asked (totvs, sap_business_one, sap, omie, sankhya, senior, linx, netsuite, dynamics, bling, tiny, contaazul, egestor, vhsys, marketup, gestaoclick, nomus), each proved with public evidence: a job post the company itself published, its site or its domain's e-mail setup. The same search, company check and filters as the "Usa ERP" signal (recruiters, accounting offices, ERP vendors and consultancies, and posts published for another company are left out), as a one-off list instead of a daily feed. Candidates come from job posts that name the ERP: Nock's job index first (LinkedIn, its largest source, read every 6 hours for posts naming the ERPs and their modules, plus Gupy, Vagas.com, Indeed, Glassdoor, Sólides and others), and when it has fewer than asked LinkedIn is searched live in the same call; then openings in an area that runs it (hiringArea: fiscal_contabil by default, fiscal, contabil, controladoria, financeiro, compras), then companies of the market (location, industry, companySizes). Filters on the job post that brought the company, read BEFORE any check (a candidate that fails them is never checked nor charged): postedWithinDays (1 to 180, only posts published within that many days; a company with no dated post is left out) and jobPostTitles (words or titles, e.g. ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"], accents and case aside; a title of several words needs each). An ask that pairs the ERP with a job post in an area always maps to these filters: "usam TOTVS e abriram vaga no financeiro de analista, coordenador ou controller nos últimos 30 dias" is hiringArea "financeiro", jobPostTitles ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"], postedWithinDays 30. With hiringArea every company delivered has a post of that area within the days (hiringPost: title, date, link; namesTheErp true when that same post names the ERP, the strongest, listed first), apart from the ERP's proof; a company without one is never delivered. Each proof is graded (evidence.grade: forte when the post requires the ERP, média when desirable, fraca when it accepts other ERPs, "ou similares", left out unless includeWeakProof true). A company is delivered only as the post's employer: never a recruiter (by name, by its CNPJ's CNAE 78.10, 78.20 or 78.30, or a post that says "nosso cliente"; its people are never returned), a hidden employer ("Confidencial") or an accounting office, never a site of another company with a similar name (checked against the Registry's CNPJ and state), and, with companySizes, never one whose headcount (the job index's or the Registry's estimate) is outside them. It also looks up one decision maker at each company (without jobTitle, the finance decision makers: CFO, diretor or gerente financeiro, controller, gerente de controladoria, area "financeiro" leaving out other areas' and recruiters' titles; at a small company with none of them, who decides there; a jobTitle names anyone else; findPeople false skips it; withEmail adds the work e-mail) and saves every company in a sheet before it returns: the ERP, the evidence excerpt and its address on the company, the decision maker as a person row of that company. sheetId adds to an existing sheet and skips the companies it already has; without it a sheet named sheetName (default "Usa <ERPs>") is reused or created. limit 10 by default, 200 at most. Two steps: without confirmed it runs nothing, charges nothing and returns maxCredits, the most the call can cost, and candidates (how many companies of Nock's job index pass the filters before any check); with confirmed true it runs and charges. Prices, only for the companies delivered (the companies checked and left out are never charged): 6 per company delivered with the ERP proved (its check and the job post read for it included); 8 per decision maker found by search (a partner the Receita names is free); 3 per work e-mail found. Finishes within about 85 seconds and returns the companies (name, domain, cnpj, city and uf from the Registry, empty when not found; ERP, confidence, evidence source, url, excerpt and postedAt; jobPost with its title, url and postedAt; decision maker with LinkedIn), counts, creditsCharged, leftOutBeforeCharge, sheetId and sheetPath. Each source runs within its own time, so a late one never takes the call; LinkedIn live starts first. The call never spends with providers more than half of what its companies can be charged: past that it stops buying job posts and paid checks (stoppedAtCostCeiling true). partial true means the time ran out, a source was late or the cost ceiling was reached before the limit ("more" says which, in plain words); continuation.call is the next call, ready (the same input with the returned sheetId brings the next companies, the ones already in the sheet are neither checked nor charged again, and this call's checks are reused free).

area.description: Optional: only decision makers of this area. "financeiro" keeps finance people (CFO, finance director or manager, a finance controller) and leaves out other areas' titles such as "Controller Jurídico"; without jobTitle it also looks for the finance titles. Left out: financeiro when jobTitle is left out too, else anyone matching jobTitle.

confirmed.description: false or absent: returns the most it can cost and runs nothing. true: runs and charges.

erps.description: Any of these ERPs (totvs, sap_business_one, sap, omie, sankhya, senior, linx, netsuite, dynamics, bling, tiny, contaazul, egestor, vhsys, marketup, gestaoclick, nomus); sap_business_one needs evidence naming Business One, sap is any SAP.

findPeople.description: false brings only the companies, no decision maker. Default true.

hiringArea.description: The area of the job post the user asks for: fiscal, contabil, controladoria, financeiro or compras (fiscal_contabil is the default search when none is asked). Pass it whenever the ask names an area ("abriram vaga no financeiro" is financeiro): then every company delivered has a post of that area within postedWithinDays (30 when left out), shown as hiringPost apart from the ERP's proof, and the ones whose own area post names the ERP come first. Without it, no area post is required.

includeWeakProof.description: true also delivers companies whose only proof is a post that accepts other ERPs ("Winthor ou similares"), graded fraca. Default false: left out.

industry.description: The sector in plain words, e.g. "indústria de alimentos".

jobPostTitles.description: Optional: only companies whose job post's title has one of these words or titles, accents and case aside, e.g. ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"] (a title of several words needs each of them). Applied before any check: a post of another title is never checked nor charged. With hiringArea they are the titles of the area's post ("vaga no financeiro de analista, coordenador ou controller nos últimos 30 dias" is hiringArea "financeiro", jobPostTitles ["analista", "coordenador", "controller"], postedWithinDays 30).

jobTitle.description: Who to find at each company, titles tried in order, comma-separated. Default: the finance decision makers ("CFO, Diretor Financeiro, Gerente Financeiro, Controller Financeiro, Controller, Gerente de Controladoria", area "financeiro").

limit.description: Companies to bring, 10 by default, 200 at most.

location.description: A state or city, e.g. "SP" or "Curitiba, PR". Brazil when left out.

postedWithinDays.description: Optional, 1 to 180: only companies whose job post was published within this many days ("abriram vaga nos últimos 30 dias" is 30). Applied before any check: an older post, or a company with no dated post, is never checked nor charged. Each company returns its post's date (jobPost.postedAt).

sheetId.description: An existing sheet to add the companies to; companies already in it are skipped. Without it, a new sheet is made.

sheetName.description: The name of the sheet to use or make when there is no sheetId (a sheet of that name is reused).

withEmail.description: Also look up each decision maker's work e-mail. Default false.
